## Validation report

### A. Sun and Earth directions against NASA JPL Horizons

- 160 fixtures at 7 landing sites (apollo11, apollo12, chandrayaan3, change6, im1, im2, slim), tolerance 0.01 deg: **PASS**, 0 outside tolerance.
- Largest gap: 0.00010 deg in azimuth (scaled by cos elevation), 0.00069 deg in elevation.
- Earth parallax between Moon centre and site: up to 0.2767 deg at the fixtures (geometric ceiling 0.2793 deg). The check fails if the site vector is not subtracted.
- Full table: section 3.
- Ephemeris rows: 70128 (hourly). Span and ranges: section 2.

### B. Long-run sunlight at Connecting Ridge against a published value

- Ours: sunlit 91.25 percent of the time (2 m mast, limb rule, hourly samples) over the whole ephemeris, 2023 to 2030, 8.0 years. Across the terrain error band: 88.18 to 93.09 percent. Computed on 15 Nov with the app's engine (`app/src/engine`) from this pipeline's `ephem.bin` and `horizon/connecting_ridge.json` (commit 8835191).
- Published: 92.27 percent at 2 m above ground (Glaeser et al. 2014, Icarus 243, 78-90, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2014.08.013), from a 19-year run on a 20 m/pixel LOLA terrain model.
- The two are not the same experiment: **different time span and newer DEM** (ours is the 5 m PGDA 78 site model inside the 80 m PGDA 90 grid), and our point is the paper's site as listed in `data-src/sites.yaml`. Agreement to about one percentage point is a plausibility check, not a numeric validation. The published value lies inside our band.

## Lead-site lines with the terrain band

Reference engine (`tests/reference/engine_ref.py`) on the real data, 10-minute samples. The range is the same stay computed on the lowered and the raised horizon.

- sunlit hours for the 7-day IM-1 Odysseus (near Malapert A) stay from 2024-01-19 23:24 UTC (baseline): 155.5 h, range 148.8 to 157.0 h across the terrain error band.
- sunlit hours for the 7-day IM-1 Odysseus (near Malapert A) stay from 2024-01-29 23:24 UTC (+10 d): 82.0 h, range 81.7 to 82.3 h across the terrain error band.
- sunlit hours for the 10-day IM-2 Athena (Mons Mouton) stay from 2025-03-06 17:29 UTC (baseline): 240.0 h, range 240.0 to 240.0 h across the terrain error band.
- sunlit hours for the 10-day IM-2 Athena (Mons Mouton) stay from 2025-03-13 17:29 UTC (+7 d): 149.5 h, range 149.3 to 149.7 h across the terrain error band.
- sunlit hours for the 10-day Connecting Ridge (Shackleton–de Gerlache) stay from 2025-03-06 17:30 UTC (baseline): 240.0 h, range 240.0 to 240.0 h across the terrain error band.
- sunlit hours for the 10-day Connecting Ridge (Shackleton–de Gerlache) stay from 2025-03-13 17:30 UTC (+7 d): 240.0 h, range 240.0 to 240.0 h across the terrain error band.

5 of 6 of these ranges are under one hour wide. The terrain height error matters for the IM-1 baseline stay and hardly at all for the others.

## One-line claims

Plain-English sentences for the page. Each uses only numbers the pipeline produced.

1. Sun and Earth positions match NASA JPL Horizons to within 0.0007° at 7 landing sites (160 checks, all inside the 0.01° tolerance): about 1/750 of the Sun's width. *Source: validation.json, horizons_check.*
2. Earth is placed as seen from the landing site, not from the Moon's centre; the difference reaches 0.28° in our checks, and the check fails without it. *Source: validation.json, horizons_check.*
3. At Connecting Ridge our model has the Sun in view 91.25% of the time over 2023 to 2030 (88.18% to 93.09% across the terrain error band); a published study found 92.27% over 19 years (Gläser et al. 2014), which lies inside our band. *Source: validation.json, benchmark.*
4. Counting the Sun only when at least half its disc shows, the Connecting Ridge figure is 86.56%. *Source: validation.json, benchmark.*
5. At the IM-1 site a 10-day slip cuts a 7-day stay from 155.5 to 82.0 hours of sunlight; with the terrain height error the baseline is 148.8 to 157.0 h and the slipped stay 81.7 to 82.3 h. *Source: validation.json, lead_lines.*
6. Every terrain horizon carries an uncertainty band built from NASA's published height-error maps; at the highest point of each skyline the band is at most 0.34° wide across 6 sites. *Source: validation.json, bands.*
7. The ephemeris comes from NASA NAIF SPICE kernels (CSPICE_N0067 via spiceypy 8.4.0, DE440) and the terrain from NASA GSFC LOLA elevation models (8 files read). *Source: validation.json, products.*

Hourly rows, 2024-01-01T00Z to 2030-12-31T23Z, frame `MOON_ME`, observer Moon centre, aberration correction `LT+S`. Row layout: Sun unit vector, Sun distance in AU, Earth position in km. The app must subtract the site vector from the Earth position.

- Sub-solar latitude range: -1.588 to 1.586 deg
- Sun distance: 0.9807 to 1.0193 AU
- Earth libration in latitude: -6.862 to 6.856 deg
- Earth libration in longitude: -8.045 to 8.052 deg

These ranges are computed from the vectors in the file, not typed in.

## 3. Validation against JPL Horizons (`fetch_horizons.py`, `check_vs_horizons.py`)

Truth: Horizons apparent, airless azimuth and elevation for an observer on the lunar surface (`CENTER='coord@301'`, geodetic east longitude, latitude, altitude). Ours: `ephem.bin`, linear interpolation between hourly rows, Sun vector renormalised, Earth = earth_km - site_km, rotated to the local frame. Azimuth gaps are scaled by cos(elevation).

Fixtures: 160 values, tolerance 0.01 deg. Sites whose catalogue elevation is missing were sent to Horizons with altitude 0 km: im2.

Earth parallax: the geocentric and topocentric Earth directions differ by up to 0.2767 deg at these fixtures (geometric ceiling 0.2793 deg). Skipping the site vector would break the tolerance.

## 4. Terrain horizons (`pipeline/make_horizons.py`, `pipeline/horizon_lib.py`)

Method: 720 azimuths, great-circle rays, Moon curvature, observer 2 m above the DEM surface at the site, range 220 km, step growing 0.4 percent per sample. The finest DEM with data at a sample wins. The occluder of an azimuth is the sample with the largest elevation angle. Beyond DEM coverage the terrain is assumed to lie on the reference sphere; where only that assumed surface sets the horizon, the occluder is null. Sites with `terrain: sphere` get a flat 0 deg horizon. For reference, the true smooth-sphere dip for a 2 m mast is -0.087 deg.

DEM sources:
- NASA GSFC PGDA product 90, https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/90, Barker et al. 2023, Planet. Sci. J. 4, 183, doi:10.3847/PSJ/acf3e1 (`LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ.TIF`, `LDEM_60S_240MPP_ADJ.TIF`, and `LDEM_80S_40MPP_ADJ.TIF` when the run used `--fine 40`).
- NASA GSFC PGDA product 78, https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/78, Barker et al. 2021, Planet. Space Sci. 203, 105119 (`Site01_final_adj_5mpp_surf.tif`, `Site04_final_adj_5mpp_surf.tif`).
- These are the track-adjusted GeoTIFF versions of the LOLA polar grids, not the PDS `.IMG` files named in the brief. Scale and offset below are the GeoTIFF's own tags.

## 5. Uncertainty bands

Each DEM is published with a per-pixel height error map in metres: `*_toterr.tif` for the PGDA 78 site DEMs (described on the product page as formally the RMS error) and `*_ERR.TIF` for PGDA 90 (described as the LDEM surface height error).

Method: the horizon is recomputed twice. Upper edge: every terrain cell raised by its error, observer lowered by the error at the site. Lower edge: the reverse. This is an envelope built from the published errors, not a stated confidence interval.

Not included: the error from the grid spacing. A grid cannot show relief smaller than its cells, which matters most where the occluder is only a few cells away. The last column gives that distance for the highest point of each horizon.

`dem.sigma_m` in each horizon file is the median error at the occluder cells.

| Site | Error at occluders, median (m) | Error at site (m) | Band half width: median (deg) | at the peak (deg) | max (deg) | Peak occluder distance (m) | Finest grid (m) |

| im1 | 0.38 | 0.773 | 0.056 | 0.1691 | 0.6672 | 400.0 | 40 |
| im2 | 0.16 | 0.136 | 0.0016 | 0.001 | 0.0843 | 16471.0 | 40 |
| chandrayaan3 | 0.462 | 0.152 | 0.0017 | 0.0026 | 0.1159 | 16080.0 | 240 |
| connecting_ridge | 0.198 | 0.375 | 0.1219 | 0.0993 | 0.7894 | 335.0 | 5 |
| shackleton_sr1 | 0.124 | 0.105 | 0.0022 | 0.0013 | 0.1768 | 9760.0 | 40 |
| shackleton_sr2 | 0.118 | 0.109 | 0.0052 | 0.0018 | 0.3284 | 8440.0 | 40 |

## 6. Feature names

`features.json` is built from `data-src/features-seed.yaml` (IAU names with USGS Gazetteer
IDs, curated by Agent C) plus two informal summits, "Connecting Ridge" and "Peak near
Shackleton", each placed at the highest pixel of its PGDA 78 site DEM. An occluder gets a
feature's id when it lies within 1.1 times the feature's radius of the feature's centre
(the margin lets a crater rim carry the crater's name). When several features contain it,
the smallest wins. A feature that contains the site itself is skipped: at a site on Mons
Mouton nearly every direction would otherwise read "Mons Mouton", which names the ground
underfoot, not an obstacle. Those ids are listed in `site_used.stands_on`. Occluders outside
every remaining feature stay null and must be shown as unnamed terrain. A name says which mapped feature the blocking terrain belongs to, not which part
of it.

## 7. Earlier checks with the same ray-marcher (run by the human on 14 Nov 2026)

These used an earlier version of `horizon_lib.py` on the PGDA 78 site DEMs plus
`LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ.TIF`. The console output was pasted into the working session; the
numbers are not regenerated by this script.

- Horizons `coord@301` check at the Connecting Ridge point over 91 daily epochs, using JPL
  Horizons sub-solar and sub-Earth points as the ephemeris: largest elevation gap 0.0012 deg
  (Sun) and 0.0010 deg (Earth); largest azimuth gap 0.0007 deg (Sun) and 0.0063 deg (Earth).
- Convergence: rays every 0.25 deg with four times smaller steps changed no site's sunlit or
  Earth-visible share by more than 0.1 percentage point; largest change on shared rays 0.014 deg.
- Cross-site check: the skyline seen from each of six polar points matched the predicted
  elevation of the other points' summits in all 30 pairs.

## 8. Known limits

- Visibility thresholds are the app's job; this pipeline only supplies vectors and horizons.
- Sites not on a 5 m DEM use 80 m or 240 m terrain, so ground within a few hundred metres
  of the lander is smoothed.
- `connecting_ridge` uses the catalogue coordinate (Gläser et al. 2014, spot 2) and the
  PGDA 78 Site01 5 m DEM for its height. That DEM is newer than the one Gläser used, so
  the published percentage is a benchmark, not a value to reproduce exactly.
